site.name: DASH
site.title: DASH Browser
site.description: DASH is a free browser for Windows and Android with no telemetry, no accounts and everything stored on your device.

hero.lede: DASH is a fast, free browser for Windows and Android. It blocks ads and trackers, sends nothing about you to anyone, and keeps your data on your own device.

connections.title: Every connection DASH makes, listed.
connections.intro: Most browsers call home for analytics, sync and suggestions. DASH has none of that. Besides loading the pages you ask for, these are the only requests it can make, and each one is off by default or starts with something you do.
connections.note: This list comes from DASH's privacy statement. If DASH ever makes a request that is not on it, that is a bug, and you can report it.

rows.title: Telemetry
rows.text: Analytics, crash reports, usage statistics, advertising IDs.

rows.title: Accounts and sync
rows.text: There is nothing to sign in to. Your history and passwords never leave your device.

rows.title: Update check
rows.text: Only the address you enter yourself.

rows.title: Secure DNS
rows.text: The DNS provider you pick (Cloudflare by default).

rows.title: Search suggestions
rows.text: Your chosen search engine, with what you type, no cookies.

rows.title: AI helper
rows.text: A model on your own computer (Ollama). Nothing goes to an online AI service.

features.title: Built for the daily grind, not for data brokers.
features.intro: The basics you expect, plus the privacy tools other browsers hide in menus.

items.title: Ads and trackers, stopped first
items.text: Requests to known ad and tracking hosts are blocked before they load, so pages are faster and nothing watches you read. Turn blocking off for one site if it breaks.

items.title: HTTPS-only mode
items.text: DASH upgrades plain http addresses to https and warns you before opening a site that cannot be secured. On Android, certificate errors cannot be clicked away.

items.title: Private tabs that clean up
items.text: Incognito uses a separate profile. When the last private tab closes, its cookies, storage and cache are wiped.

items.title: Passwords, encrypted
items.text: Saved logins are protected by your operating system's secure storage and can be locked behind your fingerprint or device PIN.

items.title: Backups you control
items.text: Export everything to one file, encrypted with a passphrase you choose (scrypt and AES-256-GCM). Move it between Windows and Android.

items.title: Keeps playing with the screen off
items.text: On Android, video and music continue when you lock your phone or switch apps, with play and pause on the lock screen. You can turn it off in settings.

items.title: On Windows, more control
items.text: Container tabs, split view, sleeping tabs, extensions from the Chrome Web Store, a proxy or VPN, web apps, a built-in password manager and an app lock.

items.title: On Android, built for one hand
items.text: Swipe the address bar to change tabs, swipe a tab card to close it (with Undo), scan QR codes, search by voice and open video in Picture-in-Picture.

items.title: Reader and translate
items.text: Strip a page down to its text, or translate it when you ask.

playground.title: Try to follow me.
playground.text: Trackers chase whatever you browse. Move your pointer and they follow. Click, tap or press Space to dash and cut the ones nearby. This is a toy, not real blocking data.

windows.title: Installing on Windows
items: If Windows SmartScreen says it protected your PC, choose More info, then Run anyway. This appears because the build is not signed yet, not because anything was detected.
Finish the installer, open DASH and pick your look and search engine.

android.title: Installing on Android
items: Open the downloaded .apk from your notifications or Downloads.
If asked, allow installs from this source, then go back and tap Install.
Open DASH. You can turn the permission off again afterwards.

items.q: Does DASH collect anything about me?
items.a: No. There is no telemetry, no account and no advertising ID. History, bookmarks, notes and passwords stay in DASH's data folder on your device. The full list of connections is above.

items.q: Why does Windows warn me before running it?
items.a: The Windows build is not code-signed yet, and Windows warns about any unsigned program from a small publisher. Compare the file's SHA-256 with the one shown here before you run it.

items.q: Can I read or change the code?
items.a: Yes. The source code is public. Under the PolyForm Noncommercial licence you can read it, build it, change it for yourself and share your changes for noncommercial purposes. You cannot sell DASH or include it in something you sell. Because of that limit it is called source-available, not open source.
Yes. DASH is free to download and use. It is made by Bibek Bista, an independent developer in Nepal. It has no ads and nothing in it tracks you.

items.q: Can I sync between my laptop and phone?
items.a: There is no sync service, because that would mean your data sits on someone's server. Instead, export an encrypted backup on one device and restore it on the other.
Windows runs on Chromium through Electron. Android uses the system WebView. Websites that work in Chrome work in DASH.

items.q: I found a bug. Where do I report it?
items.a: Use the Report a problem link in the footer. Security problems go through the private route described on the Security page.

cta.title: The data a browser collects is hard to take back. Start by giving it none.
cta.text: Free. Private. Yours. It takes about two minutes.

footer.text: A privacy-first browser by Bibek Bista, an independent developer in Nepal. Free to use.

home.manifesto: Most browsers are paid for by watching you. DASH is free and made by one developer, and it is built so that nothing in it depends on watching you. It blocks the trackers, keeps everything on your device, and lists every connection it can make.

peek.title: This is what any website can read about you. Right now.
peek.intro: No click needed. Your browser hands this to every page you open, and trackers collect lists like it, then match them across sites. We read it here, in your own browser. This page sent none of it anywhere.
peek.foot: DASH stops known tracker hosts from loading at all, so those scripts never get to ask. It also sends the Global Privacy Control signal by default. No browser can promise you anonymity, and DASH does not.

items.title: Free, and no catch
items.text: No account and no ads. DASH does not make money from your attention, and it does not need to know who you are.

items.title: Check it, don't trust us
items.text: Every connection DASH can make is listed in plain words, and the code is public. If we ever change that, the history shows it.

items.title: Ready in two minutes
items.text: Install, pick a theme and a search engine, bring your bookmarks from a file or another browser, and go. Nothing to sign up for first.

switch.title: Switch in three steps
switch.sub: You can keep your old browser installed. Try DASH for a day and see.

items.d: Pick Windows or Android. The file comes straight from GitHub.
On Windows you may see a warning because the build is not code-signed yet. The steps on the Download page show exactly what to click.
On desktop, import bookmarks and more from another browser in Settings, or from a file on the welcome screen.

developer.name: Bibek Bista
developer.sub: I'm Bibek. I design, write, test and ship DASH on my own, from Nepal. The code is public to read, and the Promises page shows how to check what DASH does on your own computer.
developer.stackText: Desktop is Electron with React and TypeScript. Android is Kotlin on the system WebView. This website is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript built by a small script. Hover the orbit to hold it still.

principles.b: Every feature is real. If something is limited or not tested yet, the release notes and this site say so.
DASH sends nothing about you to me or anyone else. I can't see who uses it or what they browse.
History, bookmarks and passwords live on your device. There is no account to sign in to.
Check what it does on your own computer, then tell me where I got it wrong.

developer.ctaTitle: Want to see what else I make?
developer.ctaText: My portfolio has my other work and a way to reach me. Found a bug or want a feature in DASH? Open an issue on GitHub, I read every one.
